title: Low fidelity wireframe before styling
when: Before building a page or app the user wants the structure agreed first: a grayscale wireframe of sections and content blocks.
prompt:
Goal: A grayscale HTML wireframe that fixes structure, content order and priorities on phone and desktop, with no styling decisions.
Steps:
1. Write the content inventory first: each section, its purpose and the one action it supports.
2. Build wireframe.html with landmarks and real headings; media are boxes labeled with what they will show (Team photo, 4:3).
3. Use grays only: #fff and #eee surfaces, #999 for borders, #333 for text, one system font, outlined buttons; no brand color or images.
4. Lay out phone first in one column, then a wide layout in a media query, so both priorities are visible.
5. Write real draft copy for headings and buttons, and short realistic sentences for body text.
6. Add numbered notes (aside class="note") for open questions and behavior, such as what happens on submit.
Quality bar:
- A stakeholder can follow the flow without help.
- Every section has a purpose line.
- Changes take minutes.
Pitfalls:
- Choosing colors and fonts at this stage.
- Filler text that hides content problems.
- Desktop only wireframes.
Verify:
- [ ] wireframe.html has one h1 and landmarks.
- [ ] Only grayscale colors, text in #333.
- [ ] Media boxes say what goes there.
- [ ] A width media query exists.
Output: wireframe.html with its grayscale styles, and the content inventory as a list at the top.

examples.input: antes de fazer o site, me mostra a estrutura das paginas
examples.output: grayscale wireframe: hero box, 3 service blocks, testimonial, contact form, notes on booking behavior
